comment: Student plan going up a dollar is rough, but I'm not leaving. It's still the cheapest way I can get ad-free for my classes.
'Best possible experience' while the app keeps getting more cluttered. Show me what I'm actually paying for.
Family at $21.99 for six accounts is still cheaper per head than anything else. Grudgingly staying.
Done. Apple Music is $10.99 and I already pay for Apple One, so this was the push I needed to move over.
I'd like to see where the extra dollar goes. Artists are still getting fractions of a cent per stream, so show the receipts.
Can't afford this anymore. Going back to the free tier and dealing with the ads again.
A dollar a month. Didn't notice anything except the email.
Everything costs more now and Spotify is still the best deal in streaming. Read the terms before you rage.
Paying more and still no lossless in the US? Tidal has had lossless for years. I'm done waiting.
They want more money while pushing audiobooks and podcasts at me every time I open the app. Just give me music at the old price.
Duo going up $2 to $18.99 with my partner. Still cheaper than two Individual plans, so we stay.
This is exactly why people stop paying. At $13 for something I can find elsewhere in ten seconds, I'm just going to stop.
YouTube Music Premium is $10.99 and includes YouTube. Spotify keeps climbing and I'm out.
Fair increase. It's been a while since the last one and the recommendations are still excellent.
Moving our family plan down to Individual now that the kids have their own accounts. Not paying more for a plan we don't need.
The app gets slower every release and keeps shoving playlists I never asked for. Raising the price on this is wild.
Netflix and Disney already did this, so it's the same story. Rent went up way more than this.
Record profits and they're raising prices again. Typical.
I'm on free and not paying anything, so this doesn't affect me.
Amazon Music Unlimited is still cheaper if you have Prime. Switching the household over this weekend.
I'm a musician on Spotify, and I doubt the extra dollar reaches me. Still staying for discovery, but the artist side needs to change.
Still no lossless after this hike. That's the real insult.
People acting like a dollar a month is the end of the world. It costs less than my Tuesday coffee.
Student plan going up and I'm out. Can't justify it between textbooks and rent.
Eh. Price goes up, I keep listening.
I mostly listen to podcasts, so this hits harder. Might cut Spotify and move the podcast habit to Pocket Casts.
Annoying, but not leaving. Discover Weekly still slaps.
$21.99 for a household that already pays for internet, phones and three other streaming services. No.
